title: Health Screening for Persons with Disabilities and Special Needs
what_it_is: Health Screening for Persons with Disabilities and Special Needs

sections.label: School health and dental services
sections.summary: HPB's School Health and School Dental Services provide screening and immunisation to students in SPED and mainstream schools.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: The Health Promotion Board's (HPB's) School Health Services (SHS) and School Dental Services (SDS) provide health and dental screening, and immunisation services to students with special needs in Special Education (SPED) schools, in addition to those in mainstream schools.

sections.label: Screen for Life programme
sections.summary: Screen for Life offers subsidised screening for chronic diseases and selected cancers to all Singaporeans, including persons with disabilities, at CHAS GP clinics.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: HPB's Screen for Life (SFL) programme, which offers age-appropriate subsidised health screening tests for chronic diseases and selected cancers are open to all Singaporeans, including persons with disabilities and special needs, at participating Community Health Assist Scheme (CHAS) general practitioner (GP) clinics.

sections.label: Outreach letters by age
sections.summary: Letters are sent at ages 25, 40 and 50 for cervical, chronic disease and cancer screening, with outreach to at-risk groups and VWOs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Second, does the Ministry intend to step up efforts to reach out to these groups of people who are at risk of suffering from, say, breast cancer or dementia, and also by working with the voluntary welfare organisations (VWOs) which are active in these areas?

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: So, one letter is sent out to females in that year when they are 25 years of age for cervical cancer screening.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: At age 40, all eligible Singaporeans will be sent a person-centric customised letter for them to go for screening for chronic diseases.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: At age 50, there is another letter for chronic disease as well as for certain cancer screening, such as mammogram, colorectal cancer and so on.

sections.label: Reminders at ages 26, 41, 51
sections.summary: Reminders are given at the ages of 26, 41 and 51.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: In fact, we give them a reminder at the ages of 26, 41 and 51.

sections.label: Programmes for disabilities and seniors
sections.summary: Campaigns like War on Diabetes apply to everyone, and special programmes at Senior Activity and Senior Care Centres serve people with limited mobility.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: So, for programmes and campaigns, say, "War on Diabetes" where we talk about healthy lifestyle, healthy diet, healthy eating, they are applicable to everybody, including those with disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: We also have some special programmes, for instance, at the Senior Activity Centres or the Senior Care Centres, physical activities for people who are not mobile, on wheelchairs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: We work with the operators of the Senior Care Centres, the VWOs and so on, to give health talks and encourage these patients to go for health screening.
